trust_decision.summary: Whether the user's Terraform Cloud/Enterprise token (and the tfr:// registry token) may be sent to a host named by the scanned, untrusted Terraform input; decided by comparing that host against the configured trusted host in hostsEqual at each token-bearing sender.

landing_point.why: The advisory's 'unvalidated hostname' is the `hostname` attribute of the scanned cloud/backend block; this is where that scanned value is written straight onto the token-bearing AuthedAPIClient (SetHost) before every authenticated Get, so an engineer reading only the summary starts here.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The file is headed 'Contents of this file were copied from github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt' and its TerraformRegistryGetter is not referenced anywhere at the pinned commit (the live tfr:// getter is tgterraform.RegistryGetter at terragrunt_hcl_provider.go:137), so it reads as vendored dead code outside the Terraform Cloud token path, and the TG_TF_REGISTRY_TOKEN it guards is a different secret from TERRAFORM_CLOUD_TOKEN.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Terraform Enterprise/private-host users must keep working: a scanned cloud block that names the configured TERRAFORM_CLOUD_HOST (e.g. tfe.mycorp.com) must still load remote variables and still fetch private modules, and per-host tokens from ~/.terraformrc must still be usable; a fix that pins app.terraform.io or refuses every non-default host breaks those legitimate cases.

O6_input_shapes: host in the remote-run URL printed by terraform on stdout (scheme+host+path, run id from the path)
tfr:// module source registry domain, including the empty-host default (defaultRegistryDomain / defaultRegistryHost())
absolute or relative X-Terraform-Get header URL
host with different case or a trailing dot (hostsEqual uses EqualFold + TrimSuffix)
two policy shapes: host configured (warn and skip / error) vs host not configured (error)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Plain (non-terragrunt) registry module download attaches the resolved registry credentials to a URL taken from the registry's service-discovery `modules.v1` value, so the bearer token can go to a host other than the one the credential was issued for.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The registry host in question is the module source host the user chose, and its .well-known/terraform.json is part of the trusted registry protocol that Terraform itself follows, so the redirect target is arguably the trusted host's own decision and not 'unvalidated hostname' input.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package from the landing point (internal/hcl/modules vs internal/hcl) and a different credential carrier (CredentialsSource/Disco rather than AuthedAPIClient); this file is not touched by the fix

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a single low-level 'send bearer token' helper that all Terraform Cloud API calls go through
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix already adds hostsEqual to this file, so a maintainer consolidating the rule would plausibly move the host check into cloudAPI itself; a sibling helper that sends the same token to a caller-supplied host is exactly this shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second credential provider whose ForHost falls back to the configured token when the requested host is unknown
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Terraform's own credential system has both a base credential set and a per-host lookup; adding a 'default to base token' fallback here is a natural-looking simplification that would send the token to an arbitrary module-source host.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second getter registration (e.g. an https/file or dependency-fetch getter) that also attaches TG_TF_REGISTRY_TOKEN
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Getters are registered in a map literal here, so adding a sibling getter for another source scheme, with the env-var token attached, is a one-line change a maintainer could make.

O9_family: CWE-522 insufficiently protected credentials: configured Terraform Cloud/registry token disclosed to an attacker-named host via unvalidated hostname input

O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.25.11 (go.mod:3); go build ./... and go test ./...; modules resolved from go.sum at build time (go mod download), so the first build needs a module proxy or cache
O10_build.project_tests: internal/hcl/*_test.go (parser, blocks, module loading against testdata dirs) and internal/providers/terraform/*_test.go cover the HCL providers and the TFC remote-variable loader; the fix adds internal/hcl/remote_variables_loader_tfc_test.go and internal/providers/terraform/cloud_security_test.go, neither of which exists at the pinned commit. Both new tests build blocks from a local temp dir and never need the network (mismatch paths return before any HTTP call).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a single check in remote_variables_loader.Load that compares config.Host against app.terraform.io (hardcoded), which blocks the report's example but breaks Terraform Enterprise users and never touches the remote-run URL host or the tfr:// registry token.

out_of_scope_notes: internal/apiclient/client.go:131 also sends a Bearer token, but it is the Infracost API key to the Infracost API, unrelated to this advisory and not pursued.
The live tfr:// getter at the pinned commit lives in the replaced dependency github.com/infracost/terragrunt (go.mod:317), which is outside this tree; only the local copied getter was read.
